accessibility:
`Tooltip` is built to
[WCAG's Content on Hover or Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html)
criterion:

- **Dismissible:** <kbd>Escape</kbd> hides a shown tooltip wherever focus is, without you moving the
  pointer or focus, and it stays hidden until the pointer or focus leaves the trigger and comes
  back, or, with `openOnTap`, until the next tap on the trigger. The key goes on as well, to
  whatever has focus, so a control in the trigger, such as a `Dropdown`, still gets its own Escape.
  Inside a `Popover` or `Modal`, one Escape hides the tooltip and closes that too, since a tooltip
  only adds to what's there.
- **Hoverable:** the pointer can move from the trigger onto a shown tooltip, straight across the gap
  between them, and it stays. A hidden tooltip, or one only `active` shows, lets the pointer through
  to whatever is under it.
- **Persistent:** no timer hides a tooltip that's hovered or focused.

And around it:

- Keyboard focus on the trigger shows the tooltip, as hover does. Focus that a click or a tap brings
  doesn't, and neither does a touch pointer, so tapping the trigger just does what the trigger does.
  `openOnTap` shows it with a tap, for a trigger with no tap action of its own.
- An `active` tooltip is always shown, whatever the pointer, focus and Escape do.
- Tooltip content has `role="tooltip"`, and `aria-hidden` while it's hidden.
- The trigger isn't linked to the tooltip with `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader doesn't
  announce the tooltip with it. Give an icon-only trigger its own name, such as an `aria-label`.
- The `dashed` style provides a visual cue that more information is available.
summary: The `Tooltip` component displays helpful information when users hover over or focus on an element. Hovering the trigger or giving it keyboard focus shows it. Touch doesn't, unless `openOnTap` is on, and neither does focus a click or a tap brings, so tapping the trigger just does what the trigger does. The pointer can move onto a shown tooltip. Escape hides it wherever focus is, without moving the pointer or focus, and it stays hidden until one of them leaves the trigger and comes back, or, with `openOnTap`, until the next tap on the trigger. The key always goes on too, to whatever has focus or a `Modal` or `Popover` around it, since a tooltip only adds to what's there.

props.name: content
props.description: Rich tooltip content (alternative to `label`), to read rather than use. Nothing in it should take focus or a click: it isn't in the Tab order while hidden, focus there isn't counted as being in the tooltip, and Escape hiding it would drop that focus. For links or buttons, use `HoverCard` or `Popover`.

props.name: active
props.description: Force tooltip to be always visible. Hover, focus and Escape leave it shown, so Escape goes on to whatever has focus, or to a `Modal` or `Popover` around it.

props.name: multiline
props.description: Allow tooltip to wrap to multiple lines.

props.name: square
props.description: Use square corners instead of rounded.

props.name: delay
props.description: How long the pointer or keyboard focus waits on the trigger before the tooltip shows, in milliseconds.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: How long the tooltip stays after the pointer and focus have left the trigger and the tooltip, in milliseconds. The pointer can move from the trigger onto a shown tooltip without one, across the default gap. A theme that raises `--bulma-tooltip-arrow-size` or `--bulma-tooltip-arrow-margin` widens the gap past what the pointer can cross on its own, so give it a `closeDelay` long enough to cross the rest.

props.name: openOnTap
props.description: Show the tooltip with a tap on a touch screen. Touch has no hover, so without this a phone or tablet never shows it. With it, a tap on the trigger shows it at once, and it stays until another tap on the trigger or the tooltip, a tap anywhere else, or Escape. The tap still does whatever the trigger does, so turn this on only for a trigger with no tap action of its own. Mouse and pen work the same either way.

props.name: tooltipClassName
props.description: Additional classes for the tooltip element.

extraProps.description: The element that triggers the tooltip.
